summary: Iteration 13 CSV Schema Import tested end-to-end. All 8 acceptance scenarios pass: tab strip toggles JSON/CSV textareas, CSV example inference matches spec (customer_id→enum, email→email, age→randomInt with min=28/max=51, region→enum with 'eu,us,apac', signed_up→dateOnly), Apply syncs the schema editor correctly, custom CSV inference matches (ip→ipv4 protocol-reserved, phone→phone authority-reserved, label→enum, amount→randomFloat), empty CSV hides preview, garbage CSV falls back to a single opaqueId column, JSON tab regression works, and mobile 390px viewport is fully usable with both tab buttons visible and the preview wrapping cleanly. No console/page errors detected.

issues: When CSV has one row and no data rows (e.g., single line of garbage), inference message reads 'empty column — defaulted to opaqueId' which is technically correct (no data rows below header) but slightly misleading UX. Non-blocking.

critical_code_review_comments: csvInference.js iterates the full CATALOG for every column and calls inRange on each sampled value — fine for small CSVs but O(catalog × rows × cols). Consider short-circuiting when a catalog spec hits 100% early. Not blocking.
context_for_next_testing_agent: CSV import UI is stable. All testids exist and behave: import-tab-json, import-tab-csv, import-csv-textarea, import-csv-preview, import-example-btn, import-apply-btn, import-close-btn. Schema editor rows populated correctly incl. field-min-*/field-max-*/field-values-* for randomInt/enum types.
